text.p: Here are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and a Bosnian Serb delegation including Bosnian Serb Prime Minister Gojko Klickovic stress need to promote ecnomic cooperation. Bosnian Serbs also talk with Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.
- U.N. administrator for Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic stress need for elections in Eastern Slavonia to be conducted freely and democratically.
- Serbian parliament to hold first regular session this year on March 17.

- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic goes to Vienna heading the Yugoslav delegation to the international conference on Brcko, talks with Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel on promotion of bilateral relations.

- Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic says almost all necessary seed, fuel and fertiliser have been secured for the spring sowing and that measures are being taken to obtain over three billion dinars needed for the sowing.
- JIK and Slavija Banks first need to be rehabilitated by the National Bank of Yugoslavia before their integration in Beobanka. Beobanka will decide on the integration at its assembly.
- Kragujevac cars produced 150 Yugo Corals on Thursday, the largest daily production this year, and plans to produce 2,500 vehicles in March.
- Serbia has decided to entrust foreign marketing agencies with the country's tourism propaganda without opening its own tourist offices abroad, says Serbian tourism minister Vladimir Ljubicic.
- Serb-Albanian round table on confidence-building will be held on Mt Brezovica from March 21 to 23.
- Belgrade students again try to crash reception held in National Museum but police prevents them from entering.
- Secretary General of International Journalists Federation Aidan White criticises NIN weekly for sacking the editor in chief Dusan Velickovic against the will of most of the journalists.
- Striking workers of the Belgrade and Serbian pre-schools decide to freeze strike until March 20 by which time the price of labour should be determined.
NASA BORBA
- Radio Television Serbia RTS takes away authorisation for use of five transmitters from BK TV limiting its broadcasts to the Belgrade city area.
- OSCE president in office Niels Helveg Pertersen proposes that Serbian authorities and opposition coalition Zajedno start dialogue in Copenhagen on March 17.

- Rifts emerge among students following the the student protest main board's decision to return to classes, chairman of the main board Cedomir Antic resigns. Students disappointed with decision jeer student leaders.

- U.N. Eastern Slavonia administrator Jacques Klein says in Belgrade the Serbs in the region should obtain their citizenship papers and participate in local elections which will be scheduled for April 13.
- Increasing pressures to "discipline" the bi-monthly DUGA are leading its journalists to seek to leave the BIGS company.
- Beobanka, the largest creditor of the company of deprtment stores Beograd, is negotiating with foreign department store chains to find a way to collect its debt.
- PTT Serbia introduces international rates on telephone and postal links with eastern Slavonia and Bosnian Serb republic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Foreign airlines show increasing interests in using Pristina airport.
